title.narrative: Contribution to the Danish Institute for Human Rights project "Responsible Business Conduct in Sub-Saharan Africa"

description.narrative: The project focuses on promoting and implementing responsible business conduct and the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights in the Sub-Saharan African region, with a specific focus on national implementation in Ethiopia and Tanzania, and on the human rights implications of the energy and digital transitions.

title.narrative: State, business and civil society actors have access to analyses, tools and guidance regarding their respective roles and responsibilities to address the human rights implications of the energy transition in the Sub-Saharan Africa.

Analyses and policy recommendations to address the human rights implications of the energy transition in the Sub-Saharan Africa region has been produced with collaboration from key state, business and civil society actors in the region.

target.value: A background paper identifying the salient human rights issues specific to the energy transition in the Sub-Saharan African region has been developed and key actors and fora involved in dialogue and policy-setting has been identified.

actual.value: A background paper was completed and an advisory group of relevant experts was constituted and engaged in the initiation of the scoping paper.

target.value: A policy briefing is published and disseminated that builds on the 2020 background paper and the expert multi-stakeholder workshop, documenting key recommendations for state, business and civil society actors to address the human rights implications of the energy transition in the region.

actual.value: Country scoping papers for Ethiopia and Kenya have been completed and a virtual workshop with civil society representatives was co-hosted with the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights to augment the scoping paper recommendations.

target.value: An expert multi-stakeholder workshop (involving participants from government, businesses, civil society, academia, etc.) has been held at regional level to identify priority policy and practice actions to address the human rights implications of the energy transition in the Sub-Saharan African region.

actual.value: Multi-stakeholder events have taken place with local stakeholders in both Tanzania and Kenya in order for stakeholders to engage on the elements described in the policy briefings.

title.narrative: State, business and civil society actors have access to analyses, tools and guidance regarding their respective roles and responsibilities to address the human rights implications of the digital transition in the Sub-Saharan Africa.

Analyses and policy recommendations to address the human rights implications of the digital transition in the Sub-Saharan African region has been produced with collaboration from key state, business and civil society actors in the region.

target.value: A background paper identifying the salient human rights issues specific to the digital transition in the Sub-Saharan African region has been developed and key actors and fora involved in digital transition related dialogue and policy-setting has been identified.

actual.value: A consultant was engaged to complete the background paper where an advisory group of relevant experts was also constituted and engaged.

A workshop session with six national human rights institutions in the Eastern-Southern African region was held to further concretise opportunities and needs when applying their mandate to the digital transition.

target.value: An expert multi-stakeholder workshop involving participants from government, businesses, civil society, academia, etc. has been held at regional level to identify priority policy and practice actions to address the human rights implications of the digital transition in the Sub-Saharan African region and subsequently a policy briefing is published and disseminated in relevant fora, building on the 2020-background paper and the expert multi-stakeholder workshop.

actual.value: Targeted NHRIs from the Eastern-Southern African region were engaged by the Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa (CIPESA) to build knowledge on the role of NHRIs vis-à-vis protecting human rights in the digital transition while a briefing note on development finance institutions and human rights in the context of the digital transition in Sub-Saharan Africa was completed for publication in 2023.

title.narrative: Relevant state, business and civil society actors have strengthened capacity on and collaboration for implementation of the UNGPs.

Documentation from multi-stakeholder dialogues demonstrates collaborative actions forward on the salient business and human rights issues for the country that have been identified in the 2017 NBA and other business and human rights studies, including with focus on the energy and digital transitions. Select state, business and civil society actors have enhanced capacity to work towards NAP development and implementation.

target.value: A multi-stakeholder workshop with a select number of participants active in UNGPs implementation has been convened and specific aims and objectives for UNGPs implementation going forward have been identified based on the discussion.

actual.value: A multi-stakeholder Advocacy Meeting and National Dialogue on National Action Plans on Business and Human Rights was co-hosted with the Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance; these provided critical opportunities to build capacity and buy-in for business and human rights among stakeholders as well as an opportunity for Tanzanian stakeholders to engage with regional and international actors and collaborators in promoting responsible business conduct in the region.

target.value: Based on the workshop, a briefing has been developed identifying salient human rights issues associated with specific issues which could include inter alia the energy and digital transitions in Tanzania, to supplement the existing NBA and other business and human rights studies.

actual.value: A multi-stakeholder meeting has been hosted by CHRAGG for development of a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights and the CHRAGG has involved the business community on responsible business conduct in the extractives, tourism and infrastructure sectors.

target.value: Capacity building and engagement with the state actors responsible for development of the NAP has been undertaken as well as engagement with the Tanzanian Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance to consolidate business and human rights priorities.

actual.value: There were significant delays in implementation due to COVID-19 but virtual engagement with the Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance and other relevant business and human rights stakeholders have taken place.

title.narrative: It is documented that relevant state, business and civil society actors have received a strengthened capacity on and collaboration for implementation of the UNGPs.

Documentation from a scoping study and multi-stakeholder dialogues demonstrates collaborative identification of salient business and human rights issues for the country and concrete recommendations for UNGPs implementation, including with focus on the energy and digital transitions.

target.value: A scoping study has been undertaken that has included an overview of the status of policy as well as identification of key stakeholders and salient business and human rights issues for the country.

actual.value: A desktop scoping study has been completed and a dialogue with the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission on the Commission’s strategic plan, highlighting opportunities for incorporating the business and human rights agenda has commenced.
Project period had not yet started.

target.value: A scoping study has been undertaken that has included an overview of the status of policy as well as identification of key stakeholders and salient business and human rights issues for the country.

actual.value: The project output was delayed by 12 months due to COVID19, the scoping study will be undertaken in 2021.

target.value: Project partners and/or other relevant stakeholders have published and disseminated analysis of legal and policy gaps in business and human rights and lessons learned have been drawn from the project.

actual.value: The project partner Addis Ababa University Center for Human Rights has completed and published a case study on human rights impacts in the floriculture sector and workshops co-hosted with project partners on how to address human rights in the floriculture and energy sectors have been held. The findings from floriculture and energy sector projects will be presented at a March 2023 multi-stakeholder dialogue workshop on business and human rights in Ethiopia.

title.narrative: Regional and global outreach on the energy and technology transitions.
Region specific analyses on the human rights implications of the energy and digital transitions have been produced and disseminated.

target.value: Development of analyses, tools and guidance on the human rights implications of the digital and energy transitions in Sub Saharan Africa.

actual.value: There has been a successful completion of all the outstanding project activities as analyses, tools and guidance has been developed related to the energy sectors of Ethiopia, Tanzania and Kenya and related to the digital sectors of Ethiopia, Nigeria, Kenyda, Ugansa, Zambia and South Africa.

title.narrative: Outcome 1: National-level implementation of the UNGPs in Ethiopia and Tanzania.
Key state actors have embarked on a process to develop policy initiatives to implement the UNGPs.

target.value: Progress towards national-level implementation of the UNGPs in Ethiopia and Tanzania

actual.value: There has been a successful completion of the outstanding project activities related to national implementation of the UNGPs in Ethiopia and Tanzania.
